narrative:
The model estimated a 34.0% probability that you would become a bad credit risk. That is not a certainty, but it was high enough under the bank’s approval policy to decline the application, meaning the bank judged the expected risk unacceptable rather than saying you are certain to default.

The most influential factor was the amount you requested. At 2,039 DM, it was well below the approved-applicant average of 3,019.64 DM, so this factor actually worked in your favor and reduced the risk estimate. The next most important factor was your checking-account position: a status in the 0–200 DM range was treated as a warning sign and pushed the prediction toward bad credit; approved applicants more often had no checking account (59.2%) than this range (18.4%). Your time at your current residence ranked third and was mildly favorable: one year is shorter than the approved average of about three years, but in your case the model treated it as reducing risk. These favorable points were not enough to offset the checking-account concern.

To improve a future application, ask the bank what would make your profile acceptable, bring updated checking-account statements or evidence of steadier balances, consider a smaller request or a guarantor, and avoid new credit applications while you strengthen your account history.
